messages.author: b12f09ad3f06c8da
messages.subject: qplot()  Error: Unknown parameters: span
parts:
I use the example code in ggplot2. Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis to plot . I encounter the error message below:
> qplot(carat, price, data = dsmall, geom = c("point", "smooth"), span = 1)
Error: Unknown parameters: span
my ggplot2 version is 2.1.0


who can tell me what happens?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: qplot() Error: Unknown parameters: span
parts:
My guess is that you're using the old book, because I can't find this in the second edition. 

In my experience, qplot() was very useful in the beginning, but it made me lazy and made learning the full ggplot2 syntax more difficult. Also, I believe that qplot was semi-recently altered to simplify its capabilities. This might explain why your line of code no longer works. 

I don't have the dsmall code from the book in front of me so I don't know how big dsmall is compared to diamonds, but with the full diamonds dataset you are over 1000 rows of data so the default will be gam instead of loess. gam does not accept the span argument so you can give it different numbers all day and it will ignore you. 

http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_smooth.html
http://www.ats.ucla.edu/STAT/r/faq/smooths.htm

These pages will give you some background. 

If you insist on using qplot(), just take the span=1 argument out of qplot and put it in stat_smooth() like so:
qplot(carat, price, data = dsmall, geom = c("point", "smooth")) + stat_smooth(span=1)

HTH,
B

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: qplot() Error: Unknown parameters: span
parts:
Hi::

This has come up before, and is a good example of why you should be
using ggplot() instead of qplot(). F The issue is that you've called
two geoms in your qplot() call, so qplot() doesn't really "know" that
span is supposed to apply to geom_smooth() rather than geom_point().
This problem disappears when you use

ggplot(dsmall, aes(x = carat, y = price)) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth(span = 1)

or alternatively, if you insist on using qplot(),

qplot(carat, price, data = dsmall, geom = "point") + geom_smooth(span = 1)

To address Brandon's question, dsmall is a random subsample from the
diamonds data, of length 1000 IIRC.

Dennis
